audit.title: SmartData Feed Addresses
audit.summary: This is a contract-address registry page whose entire reason to exist — the network-by-network list of SmartData feed addresses — is **client-side rendered and absent from the served HTML** (the content reads "Loading..." with 0 hex identifiers and 0 numerals). Its schema/metadata layer is genuinely strong (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList`, canonical, full OG/Twitter), but an engine or coding agent retrieving this page gets almost nothing extractable: the addresses that make it useful never appear as text. The single highest-lift fix is to server-side render (or statically embed) the address table so networks, feed types, and hex addresses are in the DOM. Until then, this page cannot be cited to answer "what is the address of feed X on network Y" — the exact query it targets.

recommendations.title: Render the address table in static HTML
recommendations.where: Under each network heading (e.g. `### Ethereum Mainnet`), currently `Loading...`
recommendations.issue: `Loading...` — the address data is client-side only, invisible to LLMs.
recommendations.change: Server-side render or statically embed a table with columns: Feed name, SmartData type, Network, **Contract address (0x…)**, decimals, proxy/aggregator. Ensure hex addresses appear as text in the DOM.
recommendations.why: Quantitative identifiers (addresses, chain IDs, decimals) are the highest-lift content type; right now the page's whole payload is unretrievable.

recommendations.title: Add per-network, symptom/query-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled `Networks` doesn't match how devs ask.
recommendations.change: Use headings like `SmartData feed addresses on Ethereum Mainnet`, `SmartData feed addresses on Arbitrum`, each with its own anchor and table, so each network is an independently retrievable chunk.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query "Chainlink SmartData address on <network>"; heading-level matches win retrieval that buried body text loses.

recommendations.title: Fix the garbled control string
recommendations.change: Render filter/column controls as real markup so the extracted text reads as a labeled table header, not a concatenated UI string.
recommendations.why: Mashed tokens degrade fluency scoring and entity resolution.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical one-sentence definition of SmartData feeds
recommendations.issue: No liftable definition; page assumes the reader already knows what SmartData is.
recommendations.change: Add e.g. "SmartData feeds are Chainlink onchain data feeds that deliver Proof of Reserve, NAV, and multi-variable asset data; each feed is a smart contract at a fixed address per network." Link to `/data-feeds/smartdata`.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-quotable anchor and a parametric-prior defense.

recommendations.title: Correct freshness signals
recommendations.issue: Identical timestamps, future-dated (2026-09-18); reads as generator-stamped, never revised.
recommendations.change: Emit a real last-updated date reflecting the last address-list change, distinct from publish date.
recommendations.why: Visible, credible freshness supports E-E-A-T; an address registry that never shows revision looks stale.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative external links per feed
recommendations.issue: 0 external/primary links; addresses unverifiable from the page.
recommendations.change: Link each address to its block explorer page (Etherscan, Arbiscan) and link the PoR risk section to the relevant methodology/spec.
recommendations.why: Inline primary-source links raise citation rate and let agents verify addresses.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal consumption snippet
recommendations.issue: No example of reading a feed at a listed address.
recommendations.change: Add a short tagged Solidity block using `AggregatorV3Interface(address).latestRoundData()` with a real listed address and imports.
recommendations.why: Turns the registry into an actionable unit agents can copy-paste.

antiPatterns: **Content wall behind client-side rendering:** the primary content renders as `Loading...`; the served page is effectively empty of its payload.
**Garbled/mashed UI text:** `SmartData TypeMore DetailsShow...` concatenates control labels into non-prose.
**Stale/undated appearance:** `datePublished == dateModified`, future-dated — reads as auto-stamped.
**Auto-templated schema entities:** `about` values are all "Content about X" boilerplate, adding no entity signal.
offPageNotes: Site-level: confirm `docs.chain.link` exposes an `llms.txt` and that this page is in the sitemap; a static address dataset (JSON/CSV) linked from here would be highly agent-friendly.
Whether the dynamic table is prerendered for crawlers is a rendering-pipeline decision (SSR/ISR) beyond page copy — flag to the docs platform team as the top priority.
The CLI should pass the fully hydrated DOM (post-JS) for a truer read; this audit reflects the served HTML, which is what most retrieval crawlers see.
